extractedRequirements.title: Internal Inventory Tracker Design
extractedRequirements.description: Design an inventory tracker tailored for a small retail shop with specific non-functional requirements and context.

database.justification: Considering team size and experience, a simpler RDBMS like PostgreSQL can be an appropriate choice for inventory tracking. It provides ACID guarantees which are beneficial in enscurating data integrity while being manageable by junior developers with proper training.

cache.justification: As the team is small and targeting low latency tolerance, Memcached can be used to cache frequently accessed inventory data in-memory. This decision aligns with high performance expectations for daily transactions while keeping complexity manageable.

messaging.justification: To ensure the system is scalable and can handle a monthly deployment without downtime, Apache Kafka as an event-driven messaging system will allow for resilience against spikes in request rate. It fits well within DevOps practices of managed services.

deployment.justification: Despite the perceived 'Distributed Systems Tax', Kubernetes can still be suitable for this scenario as it provides self-healing and scaling capabilities. Using a Platform as a Service (PaaS) with managed services will alleviate operational complexities while allowing some degree of scalability.

observability.justification: The ELK stack for logging and monitoring is recommended. It provides comprehensive observability features to detect, diagnose, and respond to system performance issues quickly due to the high latency tolerance requirement.

security.justification: For compliance with GDPR and data protection laws without adding significant operational burden on a junior team, employing managed identity services will provide secure access control to resources. PaaS options like AWS IAM can automate permission management.

triggeredRules.justification: Microservices introduce a 'Distributed Systems Tax' that is too high for small teams.
Reduces the operational burden of managing Kubernetes clusters or hardware.
Legal requirement to protect sensitive user information at rest and in transit.
